attempts.summary: Joined node2's and node3's segments (attached to node1's eth1 and eth2 respectively) into a single L2 domain via a Linux bridge (br0) on node1, with STP off. node2 (ens7) and node3 (ens7) were assigned 192.168.50.11/24 and 192.168.50.12/24 in the same subnet, persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-ens7.cfg. node1's br0 has no IP address and performs pure frame forwarding rather than routing, confirmed by matching ICMP TTL=64 (unchanged) and ARP tables on node2/node3 showing each other's real MAC addresses directly (not node1's). Bridge setup was made persistent across reboot via a new systemd unit (l2-bridge.service) enabled at boot on node1, since SONiC's interfaces-config.service only manages eth0 and does not conflict. Segment mapping (eth1->node2, eth2->node3) was empirically confirmed via targeted tcpdump capture during broadcast pings before wiring the bridge. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (node2, then node3, then node1 last since it disrupts both segments), each showing a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id post-restart, and full bridge/connectivity recovery was verified afterward (bridge forwarding state, br0 addressless, and successful bidirectional ping node2<->node3 with ARP entries showing direct peer MACs).
